obligation: TSA cybersecurity incident report to CISA
trigger: Cybersecurity incident involving IT or OT: unauthorized access, malicious software, denial of service, physical attack on network infrastructure, or any other incident that results or could result in operational disruption (includes incidents under investigation)
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after the company identifies the cybersecurity incident
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472), stating the report is made under the SD; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - TSA-designated owner/operator (PS-1, PS-2, JV-1; PS-3 under the amended plan)

obligation: TSA report supplement
trigger: Required report content (contact, affected pipelines or facilities, description, impact, responses planned) not all available in the initial report
deadline: Initial report within the 72-hour window; supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available
notify: CISA Central
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: TSA Cybersecurity Coordinator availability
trigger: Any time
deadline: Coordinator or an alternate accessible to TSA and CISA 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
notify: TSA and CISA (contact details on file with TSA)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: SSI released to unauthorized persons
trigger: Exfiltrated data includes SSI (plans, assessments, or reports submitted to TSA)
deadline: Promptly
notify: TSA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SSI was taken or exposed

obligation: PHMSA immediate telephonic notice of an incident
trigger: An incident under 191.3: a release of gas with a death or in-patient injury, estimated property damage at or above the 191.3 threshold ($122,000 in the rule text; PHMSA posts inflation adjustments), or unintentional gas loss of 3 million cubic feet or more; OR an event significant in the judgment of the operator (191.3 paragraph (3)). A cyber-caused precautionary shutdown of a pipeline system may be judged significant even with no release
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, but no later than one hour after confirmed discovery
notify: National Response Center by telephone (800-424-8802)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Vice President, Pipeline Safety and Compliance decides; the default for a cyber-caused shutdown of a pipeline system is to report
owner: Vice President, Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: PHMSA revision or confirmation of the telephonic notice
trigger: An incident reported under 191.5(a)
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable
notify: National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made
owner: Vice President, Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: PHMSA written incident report (transmission)
trigger: An incident required to be reported under 191.5
deadline: As soon as practicable but not more than 30 days after detection; supplemental report as soon as practicable when more information is obtained
notify: PHMSA portal (Form PHMSA F 7100.2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made
owner: Vice President, Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: Emergency notice to 9-1-1 centers and public officials
trigger: A gas pipeline emergency, including a shutdown or loss of supply that creates a hazard or that local officials must plan for
deadline: As the emergency plan provides; immediate and direct notice where 192.615(a)(8) requires it (for example after a notification of potential rupture)
notify: Public safety answering points (9-1-1 centers), fire, police, and other public officials along the affected system
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the event creates an emergency
owner: Vice President, Gas Control with field operations

obligation: Posting of service outages and reductions
citation: 18 CFR 284.13(d)(1); posting standards under 18 CFR 284.12; company FERC gas tariff
trigger: Planned or actual service outage or reduction in service capacity on a pipeline system
deadline: Post on the informational postings website; timing and notice content follow the tariff and the posting standards incorporated by 284.12 (not restated here)
notify: All shippers and the public through the informational postings website; affected shippers directly under the tariff
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - interstate pipeline
clock_starts: Decision to curtail or shut down

obligation: Interconnect and JV owner operational notices
citation: Interconnect operating agreements; JV operating agreements (contractual)
trigger: Curtailment, shutdown, or loss of SCADA data at shared points; any incident affecting JV-1 to JV-3
deadline: Per agreement; before any planned curtailment and as early as possible
notify: Interconnecting pipelines, LDC and power plant gas control desks, JV owners
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
clock_starts: Decision to curtail or incident affecting a JV
owner: Vice President, Gas Control; Vice President, Contract Operations

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.8)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (employee and former employee records in HR and payroll systems; shipper contact data)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company
trigger: Vendor that maintains personal information has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employees, former employees, and dependents in HR and payroll data)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
owner: General Counsel with the Chief Human Resources Officer

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 38 suppliers hold employee personal information; the payroll and HR SaaS contract still says 30 days (P03 G-133)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (supports OFAC mitigation and investigation)
notify: FBI field office or IC3 (CISA receives the SD 01G report separately)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier hotline before engaging vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline; broker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SOC 2 user entity communication
trigger: Incident affecting the shipper services platform (SL-1) or contract operations for JV owners (SL-2)
deadline: Per agreement
notify: Shippers using SL-1; JV owners (SL-2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
clock_starts: Determination that the service line is affected
owner: Vice President, Commercial Operations; Vice President, Contract Operations

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered (above the SBA size standard). SD 01G reporting continues
clock_starts: n/a until a final rule takes effect

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a registered entity with high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination; by the end of the next calendar day for an attempt to compromise; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
notify: E-ISAC and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a NERC-registered entity; no Bulk Electric System assets

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report
trigger: Electric emergency incidents and disturbances, including cyber events, as defined in the form criteria
deadline: Emergency Alert (criteria 1-9): within 1 hour; Normal Report (criteria 10-13): within 6 hours; Attempted Cyber Compromise (criterion 14): by the end of the next calendar day after determination; System Report (criteria 15-27): by the later of 24 hours after recognition or the end of the next business day; final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no electric operations

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article found in a system used under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts identified; recheck if one is signed
